proposed_english: the rooted one / be rooted, be firmly fixed
rationale: Recurring on this page in synonymous parallelism with ⲥⲙⲁⲛⲧ 'be established.' The qualitative form ϩⲟⲩⲏⲥ describes a state of being firmly anchored within a higher source. Likely Lycopolitan reflex of an organic-fixing verb (possibly cognate with ϩⲱⲣϣ̄ 'be heavy/firm' or ⲱⲗⲥ-stem 'be set fast'). 'Rooted' captures the organic register and is distinct from the architectural 'established' (ⲥⲙⲁⲛⲧ).

Greek loanword βουλεύω 'deliberate, take counsel' substantivized. The 'abode of the counsels' (ⲡⲧⲭⲁⲓ ⲛⲓ̈ⲙⲙⲟⲩⲗⲉⲩⲉ) is the Greatness as the dwelling of the divine deliberations. Distinct from ⲡⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ ('counsel' as one of the five faculties) — this is the act/content of counseling, not the faculty.
Lycopolitan reduction of ⲡⲉϥϯⲟⲩ ⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ 'his five members.' Confirmed by the immediately following enumeration of the canonical five faculties. Not to be confused with ⲡϥⲧⲟⲟⲩ '(the) four.'

From the standard qualitative ⲥⲙⲁⲙⲁⲁⲧ 'blessed' (cf. ⲡⲡⲁⲡⲉⲁⲩ ⲉⲧⲥⲙⲁⲙⲁⲁⲧ in vocabulary). Substantival use as a divine epithet — likely of the Father of Greatness here, the source of the great members of light.
= ⲥϯⲛⲟⲩϥⲉ 'sweet smell, fragrance.' In the Manichaean correspondence schema of the Father's five great members, the second IS a fragrance — direct sensory-correspondence.

Lycopolitan reflex with epenthetic ⲥ- of ϩⲣⲟⲟⲩ 'voice.' Cf. ⲍⲣⲁⲩ ('voice') in accumulated vocabulary; same root with onset variation. The third of the Father's five great members IS his beautiful voice.
